conviction_note: Nothing company-level turned up that the price does not already hold. bar: Company Q3 FY26 guide: revenue $2.465-2.490bn (0-1% cc), non-GAAP op income $295-305m, non-GAAP EPS $2.65-2.77; FY26 revenue $9.925-10.025bn, EPS $10.83-11.18, adj FCF $630-650m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001803599/000180359926000133/exhibit991q22026.htm). I size against revenue at the guide midpoint and the $2.71 EPS guide midpoint. The stock trades on the FY/Q4 guide, not on the quarter.

findings.finding: The print arrives with 18.2% of float short (7.95 days to cover, settlement 09-15), after a 17.4% fall in five sessions that no filing, downgrade or peer print explains, against a balanced skew (-0.45). If the release simply holds the FY guide, short covering is a mechanism for an upside move.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Positioning has never produced an upside reaction here: 6 of the last 7 prints fell (-11.2, -19.85, -3.21, -13.33, -6.2, +42.38, +2.76). An in-line Q2 EPS ($2.63 vs $2.64) with a guide cut went -11.2%/-22% AH. The only large up move, +42.38% in March 2025, came off a similarly depressed base.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is public, so the positioning itself is in the price. What may not be priced is the reason for the last five sessions of selling: GuruFocus's 09-25 write-up of the -7.86% day names no catalyst, there has been no analyst action since 06-30 (MarketBeat 09-08 and 09-22), consensus has been unchanged for 30 days, and peers were down only 3.2% over the month against CNXC's -9.9% (StockStory 09-28). If the fall reflected new information, estimates or targets would have moved, or the skew would be bid to puts. Neither happened. That leaves the fall looking like positioning into the print. LESSONS rule 5 says that is worth close to 0, hence the small size.
findings.independence: Two sources say the drawdown had no named cause: GuruFocus 2026-09-25 (https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9098030/concentrix-cnxc-shares-drop-786-amid-continued-downtrend) and StockStory 2026-09-28 (https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nasdaq/cnxc/news/earnings/concentrix-cnxc-q3-earnings-report-preview-what-to-look-for). Neither is independent evidence of a squeeze; both only show an absence of news.

outside_window.finding: GBL (via Sapiens) still holds 2,773,667 shares (4.55%) after a 6m-share Rule 144 block at $22.25 on 2026-04-29, and is below the 5% reporting line. Any further selling can happen without a 13D and on no dated catalyst, so it does not resolve inside the window.

baseline_tension: The only surviving lean is a small positive from a crowded short into an unexplained drawdown. It runs against the name's reaction history (6 of 7 prints sold) and gets no support from the skew, which is balanced. The price, the option market and the history already hold everything else found, so the honest reading is close to zero.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0) and rule 1 (6 of 7 prints sold): the positioning finding is cut from +1.0 to +0.4 and the emitted move from +0.8 to +0.3.

Rules 5 and 6: the FX tailwind finding (+0.2) is dropped. It is macro-to-company inference, it sits inside the guided revenue range, and it is on a reported-quarter line this name does not trade on. It now sits in searched_and_found_nothing, and print_vs_bar_pct goes from +0.2 to 0.0.

Rule 6: the bar is stated. Revenue has two agreeing sources plus the guide, while EPS is disputed ($2.40/$2.71/$2.81), so revenue and the guide midpoint are the anchor. Accenture's 10-01 print goes in outside_window.
Rule 7: short interest was checked before sizing. The name is a crowded short, which is why no negative finding was filed.
Left standing: the search result that nothing company-level is unpriced.
